subject: Operations
title: Natural Disasters and Global Chains
description: A micro-lesson that makes Natural Disasters and Global Chains usable.

hook.text: Japan's 2011 tsunami halted auto production worldwide. A 9.0 quake in one country froze factories on every continent.

buildup.text: Natural disasters—earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, volcanoes—can destroy facilities and block transportation routes.

discovery.text: Global chains amplify the impact: a disruption in one location cascades through interconnected supply networks.

twist.text: Companies often don't know they're exposed until disaster hits. Sub-tier suppliers in risk zones are invisible.

climax.text: After 2011, Toyota mapped its supply chain 10 tiers deep and built inventory buffers for critical components.

punchline.text: Map your risk before nature maps it for you.

quiz.question: What did Toyota do after the 2011 tsunami?
options: Mapped its supply chain 10 tiers deep
